newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian blue chips hit record highs.
newsitem.headline: Russian blue chips hit record highs.

text.p: Many leading Russian shares rose to record highs in active trading on Monday on strong Western demand in a thin holiday market, dealers said.
The Russian Trading System 24-share index rose 3.04 percent to a near record 219.86 on very heavy volume of $40 million. It hit a record 227.79 on July 4, 1996.
"Positive shifts on the market are obvious," said Dmitry Starenko, chief trader of Regent European Securities.
"New money has come in, maybe from the old players. There is simply total buying, and customers have shown they want other levels."
But dealers said prices would lose some ground in reaction to the sharp rise in the next few days.
"I'm expecting a correction pretty soon. Even today I saw the first big Western sellers taking profits," Starenko said.

The fact that prices retreated from their highs after news President Boris Yeltsin had cancelled some meetings because he had a heavy cold and temperature showed the market was susceptible to profit-taking, said Trinfiko trader Grigory Pinsky.
"People are no longer speculating upwards and prices have begun to fall gradually. The slightest excuse now can be used to start selling," Pinsky said.
"I think there will be very few people after the holidays who will be able to resist selling and taking profits."

LUKoil ordinaries rose to $13.00 from Sunday's closing $12.25. Mosenergo rose to $1.100 from $1.055, UES to $0.105 from $0.096 and Irkutskenergo to $0.153 from $0.150. Sunday was a working day in Russia after a four-day New Year holiday, and the market is closed again on Tuesday for Orthodox Christmas.
Dealers said demand was particularly marked for shares of companies which have issued American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Surgutneftegaz, which rose sharply on Sunday ahead of its planned ADR issue, rose as high as $0.550 on Monday from Sunday's closing $0.501 but did not reach Sunday's intrasession high of $0.570.
